name: IBPS PO
tagline: Common recruitment for Probationary Officers / Management Trainees in public sector banks

overview.about: IBPS conducts the Common Recruitment Process (CRP PO/MT) for participating public sector banks. Selection is through Prelims, Mains (objective + descriptive) and an interview; final allotment uses Mains and interview marks in an 80 : 20 ratio.
eligibility: Graduation in any discipline; mark sheet/degree must be held by the date given in the notification
Age 20–30 years (e.g. born between 02.07.1995 and 01.07.2005 for the 2025 cycle); relaxation: SC/ST 5 yrs, OBC-NCL 3 yrs, PwBD 10 yrs, ex-servicemen 5 yrs
Indian citizen (or other categories as defined)
Computer literacy and knowledge of the official language of the state are desirable

pattern.note: Sectional + overall cut-off; −0.25 per wrong answer
Minimum 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD); final = Mains 80 : Interview 20

topics.t: Number system — divisibility, HCF & LCM, remainders, unit digits
Number series — missing number, wrong number, new-pattern (all types)
Data interpretation — table, bar, line, pie, radar & mixed charts
Caselet DI, missing DI & arithmetic DI
Logical reasoning — course of action, cause & effect, inferences, strengthen/weaken

syllabus.section: Computer Aptitude (check the current notification for its section)

topics.t: MS Office — Word, Excel, PowerPoint & shortcuts
Vocabulary — synonyms, antonyms, idioms & phrasal verbs
Banking history, structure & types of banks
Regulators & financial institutions (SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, NABARD, SIDBI, EXIM, NHB, NPCI, DICGC)
Financial markets — money, capital, bond & forex
Banking products, terms & the Negotiable Instruments Act
Government schemes (credit, farm, health, housing, savings)
Union Budget, fiscal terms & Economic Survey basics
Current affairs & static GK — sources and method

cards.title: Sectional cut-offs everywhere
cards.body: Unlike SBI PO Prelims, IBPS PO applies **sectional and overall cut-offs** in both Prelims and Mains. A brilliant Quant score cannot rescue a weak English score. Your plan must keep every section safely above its cut-off.

cards.title: Final merit
points: Mains (out of 225) and Interview (out of 100) are combined 80 : 20
Final = (Mains/225) × 80 + (Interview/100) × 20
Prelims marks are not added

cards.title: GA: biggest marks per minute
cards.body: In the 2025 pattern GA gives **50 marks in 25 minutes**, and some questions carry 2 marks. Six months of current affairs plus static banking (this core syllabus) is the highest-return preparation for Mains.

cards.title: Prelims order
cards.body: English first is common because it is the section most people find hardest to time well; but the best order is the one you have tested in at least 10 full mocks. Never change it on exam day.

cards.title: Bank allotment
cards.body: After the final merit list, IBPS allots candidates to participating banks based on **merit and the preference order** you give. A provisional allotment list is published; reserve lists may follow.

cards.q: A candidate scores 135/225 in Mains and 50/100 in the interview. Final score?
In the revised (2025) IBPS PO Mains, the General/Economy/Banking Awareness section has:
cards.explain: The 2025 notification lists 35 questions for 50 marks in 25 minutes.

notes.p:
IBPS conducts a common recruitment for Probationary Officers in participating public sector banks. There are three stages: **Prelims**, **Mains** (objective + descriptive) and **Interview**. A key difference from SBI PO: IBPS applies **sectional and overall cut-offs** in both Prelims and Mains, so every section must be cleared.

Prelims marks are not counted in the final merit. The final score combines **Mains (out of 225)** and the **Interview (out of 100)** in the ratio **80 : 20**.
points: Prelims: English, Quant, Reasoning; sectional timers; sectional + overall cut-offs.
Mains: objective sections plus a descriptive paper; total 225.
Interview: 100 marks; minimum qualifying score required.
Exact section-wise pattern is revised often; check the latest IBPS notification.

notes.p:
Formula: **Final = (Mains ÷ 225) × 80 + (Interview ÷ 100) × 20**.

**Example 1:** Mains 90/225, Interview 60/100.
Mains part = 90 ÷ 225 × 80 = 0.4 × 80 = **32**.
Interview part = 60 ÷ 100 × 20 = **12**.
Final = **44/100**.

**Example 2:** Mains 135/225, Interview 50/100.
135 ÷ 225 = 0.6 → 0.6 × 80 = **48**; 50 × 0.2 = **10**; Final = **58**.

**Value of one mark:** one Mains mark = 80 ÷ 225 ≈ **0.36**; one interview mark = **0.2**. Mains dominates the final list.
Because each section has its own cut-off, the best plan is **safe scores everywhere** rather than a very high score in one section.
points: Identify your weakest section from mocks and give it daily practice time.
In Prelims, aim comfortably above previous sectional cut-offs in every section.
In Mains, GA gives high marks per minute (in the 2025 pattern, 50 marks in 25 minutes); revise current affairs and static banking every day.
Test your section order in at least 10 full mocks before exam day.

notes.p:
A wrong answer costs **¼ of the question's marks**. In Mains GA, where some questions carry more than 1 mark, a wrong answer costs more in absolute terms.

**Example:** If a GA question carries 2 marks, a wrong answer costs 0.5. Guess only after you have eliminated at least two options; a blind five-option guess has an expected value of zero and only adds risk.

After the final merit list, IBPS **provisionally allots** candidates to participating banks based on **merit, category, vacancies and your bank preference order**. Fill preferences carefully: you may be allotted to any bank you list. A reserve list may be used later for vacancies left unfilled.
Avoid these.
points: Ignoring English because 'cut-offs are low' — it is still a sectional barrier.
Starting Mains GA preparation after Prelims.
Assuming Prelims marks count in the final list.
Weak descriptive preparation; it is part of the 225.
Careless bank preference listing.

notes.p: Key points.
points: Sectional + overall cut-offs in Prelims and Mains.
Final = (Mains/225) × 80 + (Interview/100) × 20.
One Mains mark ≈ 0.36 final marks; one interview mark = 0.2.
GA: high marks per minute in Mains.
Negative marking: ¼ of question marks.
Allotment by merit + preference.

cards.title: Format
cards.body: **2 questions, 25 marks, 30 minutes**, typed in English, right after the objective test. One essay and one letter is the usual combination. It is evaluated only for candidates who clear the objective cut-offs.

cards.title: Formal letter layout
points: Sender's address, date
Receiver's designation and address
Subject line
Salutation → body (3 short paras) → complimentary close
Name/signature

cards.title: Essay in 250 words
points: Intro with one fact or definition
Two body paragraphs: opportunities and challenges
Way forward with 2–3 concrete steps
One-line conclusion

cards.title: Time split
cards.body: Spend about **2 minutes planning** each answer (jot 4–5 points), 11 minutes typing, and the last 2 minutes checking spelling and word count. Unfinished answers lose more marks than slightly shorter ones.

cards.title: Topics to prepare
cards.body: Public sector bank consolidation, UPI and digital rupee, cyber fraud, MSME credit, financial literacy, climate finance, AI in banking, women-led development. Keep 3 facts ready for each.

cards.q: The IBPS PO descriptive paper consists of:
cards.explain: Essay and letter writing: 2 questions for 25 marks in 30 minutes.

cards.q: Which element is NOT part of a standard formal letter?
cards.explain: Hashtags belong to social media, not formal letters.

notes.p:
The IBPS PO descriptive paper has **2 questions for 25 marks in 30 minutes**, typed in English, held right after the objective Mains test. The usual combination is **one essay and one letter**. It is evaluated **only for candidates who clear the objective cut-offs**, and you must also score the minimum qualifying marks in it.

Markers look at **relevance, structure, grammar, vocabulary and word limit**. Neat, well-organised answers score better than long, unstructured ones.
points: Plan 2 minutes per answer, type 11 minutes, review 2 minutes.
Respect the word limit stated in the question.
Use short paragraphs and simple sentences.

notes.p: Learn one layout and use it every time.
points: Sender's address and date (top left).
Receiver's designation and address.
**Subject:** one clear line.
**Salutation:** Sir/Madam,
**Body:** three short paragraphs: purpose → details → request/action.
**Complimentary close:** Yours faithfully (to an unknown person/office) or Yours sincerely (to a named person).
Name and signature.

notes.p:
**Question:** Write a letter to the branch manager complaining that money was debited from your account for a failed ATM transaction.

**Paragraph 1 (purpose):** I hold savings account no. XXXX at your branch; I am writing about a wrong debit of ₹5,000 on 12 August from a failed ATM withdrawal.
**Paragraph 2 (details):** the ATM location and time, the fact that no cash was dispensed, and that the amount has not been reversed after several days.
**Paragraph 3 (request):** please investigate and reverse the amount, along with any compensation due under RBI's rules for failed ATM transactions; attach the transaction slip.
**Close:** Yours faithfully, name, mobile number.
This plan takes under 2 minutes and makes the typing fast.

Use the **intro – body – way forward – conclusion** model.

**Topic: 'Financial literacy among young Indians'**
**Intro:** define financial literacy; note that digital access has grown faster than financial understanding.
**Body 1 (opportunities):** UPI, mutual funds and insurance are easy to access; early saving builds wealth.
**Body 2 (challenges):** easy credit apps, online fraud, lack of budgeting habits.
**Way forward:** financial education in college curricula; bank and RBI awareness campaigns; simple product disclosures.
**Conclusion:** one balanced line on informed choices.

Keep 3 facts ready for each common topic: PSB consolidation, UPI and digital rupee, cyber fraud, MSME credit, climate finance, AI in banking, women-led development.
Easy marks lost here.
points: No subject line in a letter.
Informal tone ('Hi', 'Thanks a lot!!').
Hashtags, abbreviations like 'u' or 'pls'.
Leaving one answer unfinished.
Spelling errors from not reviewing.

notes.p: Key points.
points: 2 questions, 25 marks, 30 minutes, typed.
Letter: addresses, date, subject, salutation, 3 paragraphs, close.
Yours faithfully (unnamed recipient); Yours sincerely (named).
Essay: intro, two body paragraphs, way forward, conclusion.
Plan 2 minutes before typing.
Prepare 3 facts per common topic.

cards.title: What the panel checks
cards.body: Communication, clarity of thought, knowledge of banking and the economy, awareness of your own background, and attitude to rural postings and transfers. The interview is **100 marks**, weighted **20%** of the final score.

cards.title: Must-prepare questions
cards.body: Introduce yourself; why banking; why leave your current job (if any); your graduation subject; your hometown's economy; current repo rate and MPC stance; one recent scheme; how you would handle an angry customer.

cards.title: Documents & DAF
cards.body: Panels often build questions from your application form. Revise every hobby and achievement you listed. Carry all original documents in the order given in the call letter.

cards.title: Qualifying marks
cards.body: You must score at least **40%** (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD) in the interview to be considered for the final merit, regardless of your Mains score.

cards.q: What weight does the IBPS PO interview carry in the final merit?
cards.explain: Mains and interview are combined in the ratio 80 : 20.

cards.q: Minimum interview score for a General-category candidate in IBPS PO is:

notes.p:
The IBPS PO interview is conducted by a panel from participating banks and IBPS. It carries **100 marks** and **20% weight** in the final score. You must score at least **40%** (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD) to be considered at all, regardless of your Mains score.

The panel checks your **communication, clarity of thought, knowledge of banking and the economy, awareness of your own background, and attitude** towards customers, rural postings and transfers.
Prepare short, honest answers (30–60 seconds) for these.
points: Introduce yourself (education, family background in one line, strengths, why banking).
Why banking? Why a public sector bank?
Why leave your current job (if employed)?
Questions from your graduation subject.
Your hometown or district's economy and banking needs.
Current repo rate and MPC stance (check the latest RBI announcement), a recent government scheme, a recent Budget point.
How you would handle an angry customer or a fraud complaint.

notes.p:
**Weak:** "My name is Arjun. I am from Nagpur. I did B.Com. My hobbies are cricket and music."
**Strong (about 45 seconds):** "Good morning. I am Arjun Deshmukh from Nagpur. I completed my B.Com from Nagpur University in 2023, where I enjoyed accounting and banking law. For the last year I have worked as an accounts assistant at a small firm, which showed me how much small businesses depend on timely bank credit. I play cricket at the district level, which taught me teamwork, and I want to build a career in public sector banking because it combines public service with long-term growth."
The strong version links your background, skills and motivation, and gives the panel easy follow-up topics.

Panels often frame questions from your **application form**. Re-read every hobby, achievement and job detail you listed. If you wrote 'reading', expect 'What was the last book you read?'.

Carry all **original documents** in the order given in the call letter, with self-attested copies. Missing documents can stop the interview from happening at all.
Avoid these.
points: Memorised answers that sound robotic.
Bluffing; it is better to say 'I am not sure, but I understand…'.
Negative comments about a past employer.
Reluctance about rural postings or transfers.
Outdated economic facts.

notes.p: Panels sometimes ask a follow-up question that you cannot answer, or challenge your answer to see how you react. Stay calm, keep eye contact and do not argue.
points: If you don't know: 'I am not sure of the exact figure, sir, but I understand the idea is…'.
If challenged: acknowledge the point, then explain your view briefly.
If asked about a weakness: name a real one and what you are doing to improve it.
Thank the panel at the end; small courtesies are noticed.

notes.p: Remember:
points: 100 marks, 20% weight.
Minimum: 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD).
Answers of 30–60 seconds; link background to motivation.
Revise everything in your application form.
Know the latest repo rate, MPC stance and one recent scheme.
Carry all originals in call-letter order.
